items.title: 2023-2026 Strategic Plan – Council
notes: Workshop #2
Report No.: CAO2023-012
Prepared By: Sandy Little

Sandy Little gave a brief introduction to the Strategic Planning process, and noted that the next public session was taking place at RIM Park on April 1, 2023 from 2:00 till 4:00 p.m. during a free skate.

Himay Antani, Manager, Deloitte facilitated the workshop and discussed the plan for the session, which included developing the core concepts Council want to put forward to create the City’s mission statement. He also responded to questions of Council.

Councillor Hanmer offered some comments on how the ideas put forward seem to be a continuation of the current mission statement, including themes of inclusion, diversity, equity, climate change, forward focused and community.
Councillor Roe offered some thoughts based on her experiences volunteering in the community. She stated that themes of community connection and welcoming to newcomers were incredibly important.

Councillor Freeman stated that some of the themes Councillors put forward on the board were almost the same things they discussed during the budget, including climate change initiatives and how to invest in them; fiscal responsibility and balancing a tax increase with individual reality; and innovation in terms of thinking differently about how the City does business.

Councillor Vasic shared some thoughts about inclusion, being less about making sure people come to us, and more about making sure there are many different spaces available. She shared that vibrancy was important, especially thinking about it through a COVID recovery lens, meeting the needs of the community to help people reconnect.

Councillor Bodaly shared additional comments around innovation. He stated that people look to Waterloo to be innovative as a technology and education city. He highlighted that the decisions Council made shouldn’t be only for the needs of the current residents, but also for residents that didn’t live here yet.

Councillor Wright offered commentary on effective engagement, and being more descriptive about what effective engagement was, especially through the lens of everything that has changed over the last term of Council. She suggested the City should think deeply about what it meant for people to participate, engage, collaborate and innovate within the City context.
Mayor McCabe shared some thoughts for the mission statement about the caring and compassionate community of Waterloo, which can mean different things to different people.

Himay Antani summarized the main themes from the board, which revolved around sustainability, equity, affordability, being forward thinking, and fiscal responsibility. He then led Council through drafting their own mission statements. Each Councillor presented their mission statements.
Mayor McCabe: Globally recognized future focused municipal leaders serving residents in a sustainable, innovative, and equitable manner.
Councillor Bodaly: Meeting the needs of current and future residents in a sustainable and equity focused manner.
Councillor Hanmer: Driving innovative, fiscally responsible, and sustainable growth supporting our inclusive and vibrant communities.
Councillor Wright: Waterloo is a future-ready community, serving its residents through collaborative and inclusive opportunities while maintaining accountability and excellence in service.
Councillor Roach: Waterloo will be recognized as Canada’s most livable city known for its innovation, inclusion, economic stability and climate responsibility.
Councillor Freeman: Working together to create a sustainable, equity focused City. To serve the public by creating an economically stable, diverse, climate resilient City.
Councillor Roe: Building a strong foundation of inclusivity through sustainability, and innovation through compassion and fiscal responsibility.
Councillor Vasic: Muddling our way through to a new normal with bold, thoughtful, and transparent leadership; by building connection across differences; and by having fun.
Council then listed off which mission statements, or mission statement themes, they thought worked best.
Sandy Little closed out the workshop by outlining the next steps for the Strategic Plan development.

notes: Streets – Proposed 30 km/h Speed
Limit Implementation Plan
Report No.: IPPW2023-001
Prepared By: Jenny Setterfield
Jenny Setterfield gave a presentation outlining the proposed implementation plan and the different options being put forward. She then responded to questions of Council.
Bob Henderson also responded to questions of Council.

Jason Thistlethwaite, Co-President, Uptown West Neighbourhood Association gave a presentation in support of Options 1 or 2b as outlined in the Staff Report. He explained how 30km/h speed limits advance many of the City’s policies. He then responded to questions of Council.
Ron Ormson also responded to questions of Council.
